items.title: 52060_Eddie Barefield oral history interview
items.q: And he was like a father to Ben Webster and I everytime we wanted to go to work.

ctx.x: Just enough so you had something to eat and a place to stay?

Right. And like in Kansas City, there was a guy in Kansas City named Piney Brown who was a patron saint of musicians. And he was like a father to Ben Webster and I everytime we wanted to go to work. We used to go to work to get our horns out of the pawnshop, and we'd go to work. And Piney took care of us, paid our rent and took us out with girls and everything. He was in the number business so we'd go out there sometimes to stay three or four days, drinking and having a ball and playing. And if Piney ran out of…
